source_review.notes: Retrieved and reviewed Gray's failure field analysis; Schneider's fail-stop paper; FLP; Chandra–Toueg failure detectors; the primary RAID and latent-sector studies; current SQLite atomic-commit assumptions; PostgreSQL 18 WAL reliability and configuration; Google SRE data-integrity and critical-state guidance; the FoundationDB architecture/simulation paper; and NIST contingency-planning guidance. Checked theorem/model scope, storage and acknowledgement assumptions, current product behavior, failure domains, correlation, operational recovery, and evidence limitations.

evidence: Checked fault, activation, error, failure, model M, safety/liveness, stop/recovery models, omission/timing/partition, corruption/Byzantine behavior, detector, domain, latency, RPO/RTO, fencing, scrubbing, and error-budget definitions.
Checked probability windows, component versus service events, time/log recovery positions, and detector-population denominators remain explicit.
Checked fault, detector suspicion, acknowledgement, persistence, repair, restoration, and semantic verification are not conflated.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Every guarantee is conditional on a boundary, assumptions, admitted faults/combinations, response, objectives, and evidence.

Reviewed the WAL conditional proof shape, quorum intersection plus persistence/fencing premises, and detector metric denominators.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Probability multiplication is explicitly conditional on defended independence; FLP and failure-detector results remain scoped to their cited models.

evidence: Reviewed process kill, OS crash, power loss, device/domain loss, restart, partitions, asymmetric delay, duplicate/reordered messages, clock faults, and timeout false suspicion.
Reviewed lost/torn/misdirected/reordered/stale/lying writes, latent sectors, silent corruption, ENOSPC, checksum coverage, rebuild, and failures during WAL/checkpoint/recovery/backup/restore.

boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: The matrix requires an explicit reason for inapplicable cells and secondary failures in recovery paths.

evidence: Checked the protected service/observable guarantee precedes mechanism and component claims.
Checked fault, error, failure, detection, containment, repair, restoration, domains, concurrency, correlation, and surviving state are recorded separately.
Checked redundancy, WAL, checksums, replication, backups, detectors, and recovery claim only their premise-bounded properties and preserve safety under uncertainty.
invariant_checking.notes: Backup existence, replica count, restart success, and timeout suspicion are never accepted as sufficient recovery or failure proof.

evidence: Reviewed guarantee implication under model M and assumptions A.
Reviewed independent quorum, complement, detector, WAL, and quorum/fencing arguments line by line against stated premises.
Reviewed why asynchronous silence cannot distinguish crash from delay and why practical progress requires assumptions beyond FLP's model.
proof_review.notes: No claim extrapolates formal results, simulation, field populations, or database documentation beyond their exact model and boundary.

evidence: The executable is labeled a finite hypothetical independence/detector model rather than field reliability evidence.
Formal theorems, empirical storage studies, current product contracts, operational guidance, simulation, injection, restore drills, and incidents are distinguished.
Crash safety, durability, availability, integrity, backup history, RPO, RTO, and security/adversarial guarantees are separately scoped.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Fault injection outside an admitted model is robustness evidence, not an automatic expansion of the proof.

evidence: Repository verification passed one standard-library Python snippet with exact seventeen-line stdout, empty stderr, zero exit status, and the recorded local Python toolchain.
Independent Decimal recomputation reproduced quorum/common-cause, drive-surface, detector, error-budget, and matrix outputs.
Thirteen source artifacts were retained under artifacts/references/DBE-071 and all local Markdown links were checked.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No live database crash, power cut, storage corruption, partition, detector experiment, deterministic simulation, restore drill, regional game day, security test, or external review was run.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed fault/error/failure causality, behavioral and domain taxonomy, stop/recovery/communication/detector models, storage integrity and acknowledgements, redundancy/common cause, software/operator/adversarial faults, objectives, testing, evidence, observability, and degradation as one framework.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed explicit commit boundaries, fencing, dependency maps, RPO/RTO and error budgets, failure-during-recovery, authoritative oracles, protected injectors and recovery credentials, canary gates, break-glass behavior, model revision, and format/protocol-compatible rollback.

pedagogical_review.notes: The chapter derives guarantees from failure assumptions, executes finite probability/detector arithmetic, covers sixteen misconceptions and ten distinct examples, and advances five exercises from definitions to elite multi-region failure-model governance with complete answers.

limitations: Internal authoring, primary/official-source, mathematical, executable-snippet, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external fault-tolerance researcher, database recovery maintainer, storage/firmware engineer, distributed-systems operator, security/adversarial reviewer, continuity owner, regulator, or educator review is claimed. The chapter and finite model prove neither real component independence or rates, durability of any storage stack, correctness of a live WAL/quorum/detector/recovery implementation, achievable RPO/RTO, coverage of correlated or adversarial faults, production resilience, certification, nor deployment fitness.
